description: Four-layer retrieval and manual reasoning expectations; no compliance claims.

cases.prompt: Four-layer stackup selection and review workflow
cases.ai_expectation: No stackup guarantees compliance. Retrieved guidance does not select CAD constraints automatically.

cases.prompt: Four-layer option with two inner ground references
cases.ai_expectation: This option trades a dedicated power plane for ground referencing; it is not mandatory for every design.

cases.prompt: Four-layer option with an inner power plane
cases.ai_expectation: The MCXA example is device-scoped; it does not make every bottom-layer route acceptable.

cases.prompt: Review the fabrication and rework cost of outer ground layers
cases.ai_expectation: NXP notes difficult rework. Surface pads and openings mean the outer copper is not a complete enclosure.

cases.prompt: Specify dielectric gaps rather than only total board thickness
cases.ai_expectation: A thicker center reduces inner-plane coupling; do not assume all adjacent copper layers are tightly coupled.

cases.prompt: Review fast signals adjacent to power copper
cases.ai_expectation: Return-path capacitors are not series data-line coupling capacitors. Do not bridge isolation barriers using this guidance.

cases.prompt: Evaluate inner-plane capacitance and discrete decoupling together
cases.ai_expectation: Four layers do not justify removing device-required decoupling capacitors.

cases.prompt: Keep vendor stackup examples and EMC heuristics conditional
cases.ai_expectation: A layer-count label or heuristic cannot certify an assembled product.

cases.prompt: Reconsider four layers when routing requirements cannot be met
cases.ai_expectation: A vendor comparison table is not a prediction that every four-layer board fails EMC.
